analysis.title: Software Trends: BofA Software CIO Survey: AI takes budget share, returns must follow
key_insights: BofA's 2H26 survey of 309 CIOs and technology budget decision makers finds AI deployment is the highest 2027 IT priority for 39.8% of respondents, more than 3x the next category (infrastructure modernization at 12.3%).
Software budgets are expected to grow 5.3% in 2027 on a midpoint-weighted basis, with IT staffing and hiring budgets up about 3.4%.
AI's share of software budgets is expected to rise from 8.3% in 2026 to 9.4% in 2027, up 14.2% YoY. About 36% of respondents expect AI to exceed 10% of software budgets, up from about 29% in 2026.
About 61% of respondents say AI funding is new budget and about 38% say it is mostly reallocation from other IT categories.

AI applications are expected to get the largest share of 2027 AI spending increases at 39.8%, followed by data platforms at 20.1%, AI infrastructure at 15.9% and AI security/governance at 14.9%. BofA says this is positive for Snowflake, which operates across all four.

Only 17.2% of respondents already see measurable enterprise-wide AI ROI and another 31.4% expect it within 12 months. 30.7% expect it in 1-2 years. BofA warns AI budgets could be cut back if ROI does not materialize.

About 85% (84.5%) plan to deploy AI agents within 12 months, but almost 60% say only 1-25% of AI pilots will convert to production next year. Only about 37% expect to move more than a quarter of pilots into production.
Cybersecurity risk (about 54%) and pricing (about 47%) are the main inhibitors of AI deployment. 46.6% are concerned about consumption-based pricing, versus 34.0% who are comfortable.

Lowest-priority areas are HCM/workforce (15.5% select it as a 2026 priority), ERP and finance (31.1%) and CRM/engagement (36.2%). BofA says this is consistent with revenue trends at the sector leaders.

Back office is the software category most often considered for AI investment (67.6%), ahead of front office (64.7%), cloud infrastructure (60.2%) and infrastructure software (55.3%). BofA reads this as CIOs looking for cost savings and headcount reductions in categories they deprioritize for budget.

Microsoft leads AI consideration in cloud infrastructure (88.4%) and infrastructure software (82.7%), and Copilot has 76.7% current or planned production use. AI labs are at about 67-70% on the same measure.

In front-office AI, AI labs lead (about 70%) and Salesforce leads traditional application vendors at 60.1%. In back-office AI, AI labs lead, followed by Docusign (58%), ServiceNow (54.5%) and Workday (about 54%).
In infrastructure AI usage likelihood, Snowflake leads traditional vendors at 51.7%, followed by ServiceNow, Atlassian (50%) and GitLab. Datadog is at 30%.

Public cloud budgets are expected to grow about 8.4% in 2027, with about 81% of respondents expecting an increase. Hybrid cloud is the most common strategy at 39.8%, followed by multi-cloud at 25.6%. 91.3% report higher AI compute usage than 12 months ago.

Cybersecurity budgets are expected to grow about 6.9% in 2027, with 86% of respondents expecting an increase. AI Security leads incremental spending domains at 60.8%, followed by identity/access management at 45.0% and data security/DLP at 38.5%.

In security vendor spending intentions, Microsoft leads at 69.3%, then CrowdStrike (35.6%), Palo Alto (22.3%) and Okta (21.0%). Cisco (29.1%), Check Point (24.9%) and Fortinet (22.0%) draw the most perceived share-loss selections, and Wiz is at 21.0%.

Weak read for HR/finance software: fewer than 16% rank HCM/workforce as a top priority, and only 7.7% say they are likely to use BlackLine back-office AI (21% among 5,001-10,000 employee firms). Paycom is at about 11% for SMB/midmarket and Paylocity about 7% for firms under 5k employees.

Existing vendors have an opening but not a lock on AI budgets: about 47% prefer AI modules from existing vendors, 36.9% are neutral and 16.5% disagree. AI labs could shift the user interface away from incumbents while accessing their data via MCP or APIs.

market_movers.rationale: Leads the survey across cloud infrastructure (88.4%), infrastructure software (82.7%) and security spending intentions (69.3%), with Copilot at 76.7% production use. BofA says it is best positioned to monetize across applications, cloud and security.
54.5% back-office AI usage likelihood, and ITSM/ITOM ranks above ERP and HCM in budget priorities. BofA says NOW can capture incremental spending through workflow automation and cost savings.
Leads traditional front-office application vendors at 60% AI usage likelihood. Incremental spending depends on competitive pricing and measurable sales and service improvements.
Leads traditional infrastructure vendors in AI usage at about 52% and operates across all four top AI spending priorities.
BofA says AI is an observability workload accelerant and Datadog stands to take disproportionate share. Infrastructure AI usage is 30%.
Scores 50% in infrastructure vendor AI usage, near the high end of peers, supporting its Rovo strategy.
AI application and data platforms take the largest share of planned AI spending increases in 2027. BofA sees a multi-year acceleration path.
Second only to Microsoft for largest cybersecurity spending increases, selected by 35.6% of respondents. AI-security and identity spending is a positive.

22.3% selected it for the largest security spending increase. The AI security and identity emphasis favors it after the CyberArk acquisition, and expected share loss at Wiz could open cloud-security opportunities.
Identity trends are positive for the pure-play identity vendors. Okta was selected by 21.0% for spending increases.
Identity trends bode well for SailPoint as an identity pure-play.
The importance of endpoint security is positive for SentinelOne and CrowdStrike.
CRM and engagement ranks in the lower quartile of spending priorities. AI projects in CRM are secondary to modernizing data estates and AI infrastructure.
ERP and finance ranked second-lowest among budget priorities, with only 7.7% likely to use BlackLine back-office AI. Consideration rises to 21% in 5k-10k employee firms.
Fewer than 16% rank HCM/workforce among top IT-budget priorities. About 11% of SMB and midmarket firms are likely to use Paycom back-office AI.
Limited near-term AI upside, with about 7% likelihood of back-office AI use among organizations under 5k employees.
Offers flexibility for customers prioritizing security through on-premises or hybrid deployments.
Provides deployment flexibility across fully managed cloud and self-managed environments.
Offers flexibility for customers prioritizing security through on-premises or hybrid deployments.
Price objective basis only: 8x CY27E EV/FCF, reflecting weaker growth, competition from AI-native entrants and a defensive AI monetization strategy.
Price objective basis only: roughly 37x CY27E EV/Sales, a 30-40% premium to high-growth SaaS peers.

sector_views.rationale: AI takes a rising share of budgets (8.3% to 9.4%) and AI applications get 39.8% of planned 2027 AI spending increases. Data platforms (20.1%) and AI infrastructure (15.9%) follow.
Budgets expected to grow about 6.9% in 2027, with AI security (60.8%) and identity/access management (45.0%) leading incremental spending.
Lowest spending priority of 11 areas (15.5%). Growth reacceleration depends on measurable benefits customers are willing to pay for.
Second-lowest budget priority (31.1%), though AI consideration is higher in large enterprises.
Ranks in the lower quartile of spending priorities (36.2%), behind data estate modernization and AI infrastructure.
Budgets expected to rise about 8.4% in 2027, with about 81% expecting higher spending.

risk_factors: Only 17.2% of respondents report measurable enterprise-wide AI ROI. If ROI does not materialize in the near-to-medium term, organizations could become more cautious about expanding AI budgets.
Cybersecurity risk (about 54%) and pricing (about 47%) are the main inhibitors to AI deployment.
Consumption-based pricing worries 46.6% of respondents, and higher usage brings less predictable and often higher costs.
Pilot-to-production conversion is uneven: almost 60% expect only 1-25% of pilots to reach production next year.
AI labs could take over the user interface and shift engagement away from incumbent software platforms, accessing their data through MCP or APIs.
The survey is a directional indicator, not an absolute indicator of spending intentions. Budget growth figures are midpoint-weighted estimates.

tension_points.theme: AI budget growth vs ROI proof
tension_points.bull_case: AI's share of software budgets rises from 8.3% to 9.4%, 85% plan to deploy agents within 12 months, and 48.6% see current or near-term ROI.
tension_points.bear_case: Only 17.2% report enterprise-wide ROI today, almost 60% expect only 1-25% of pilots to reach production, and 46.6% have reservations about consumption pricing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If ROI fails to materialize over the near-to-medium term, organizations could become more cautious about expanding AI budgets.

tension_points.bull_case: Incumbents hold workflows, data relationships, governance and business context, and about 47% prefer AI modules from existing vendors.
tension_points.bear_case: AI labs lead front-office (about 70%) and back-office AI usage likelihood and could shift user engagement away from incumbents while accessing their data through MCP or APIs.

theme_stances.key_argument: AI is taking a larger share of software budgets, funded by both incremental budgets and reallocation.
theme_stances.evidence: AI is taking a larger share of software budgets

theme_stances.key_argument: HCM, ERP and CRM rank lowest in spending priorities, trends well reflected in sector leaders' revenue trends.
theme_stances.evidence: the areas with the lowest spending priorities are CRM, ERP and HCM/Workforce

theme_stances.key_argument: AI security and identity lead incremental cybersecurity spending, favoring CrowdStrike and Palo Alto.
theme_stances.evidence: AI security and identity leading the spending priorities
